builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Learn the Directions, Normalize the Gains: Post-Training Normalization for LoRA
summary: LoRA-Norm replaces post-hoc spectral pruning and gradient-guided editing of trained LoRA adapters by rebalancing the singular values of the learned update via a fixed nonlinear transformation followed by nuclear-norm restoration, keeping learned directions and total spectral mass. It costs nothing at inference, requires no calibration data or additional training, and adds only a one-time offline spectral decomposition of each adapter. It can fail if adaptation imbalance is not the limiting factor on the reader's tasks, since gains are reported on only two backbones and three tasks, and the stronger functional equalization variant showed no consistent benefit, indicating the improvement may be task-dependent.
rationale: The method is essentially free to apply and fits constrained infrastructure, but its benefit is supported by a single study on a limited set of backbones and tasks, so it warrants a cheap workload-specific trial rather than unconditional adoption.
technique: LoRA-Norm: post-training singular-value normalization of LoRA adapters

claims.statement: LoRA-Norm replaces post-hoc spectral pruning and gradient-guided editing of trained LoRA adapters by rebalancing the singular values of the learned update via a fixed nonlinear transformation followed by nuclear-norm restoration, keeping learned directions and total spectral mass. It costs nothing at inference, requires no calibration data or additional training, and adds only a one-time offline spectral decomposition of each adapter. It can fail if adaptation imbalance is not the limiting factor on the reader's tasks, since gains are reported on only two backbones and three tasks, and the stronger functional equalization variant showed no consistent benefit, indicating the improvement may be task-dependent.

Across two backbones and three adaptation tasks, improves both average specialization and capability retention relative to post-hoc spectral pruning and gradient-guided editing; no quantitative magnitude is reported in the abstract.
